subject: Economics
description: Planning Commission, NITI Aayog, 5-year plans, key economists

questions.stem: India's FIRST Five-Year Plan (1951-56) focused mainly on:
questions.explanation: 1st FYP (1951-56) — based on Harrod-Domar model. Focus: agriculture and irrigation (Bhakra Nangal, DVC). PM Nehru was plan chairman. Target growth: 2.1%; achieved: 3.6%. Planning Commission was created in 1950 (non-statutory body).
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The SECOND Five-Year Plan (1956-61) was designed around the:
questions.explanation: 2nd FYP (1956-61) — based on the Mahalanobis (P.C. Mahalanobis) model emphasising rapid industrialisation, especially heavy industries. Led to setup of public-sector steel plants at Bhilai, Rourkela, Durgapur. Nehru-Mahalanobis strategy. heavy industry emphasis.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The PLANNING COMMISSION was REPLACED by NITI Aayog on:
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) set up 1 January 2015 by Cabinet resolution. PM is ex-officio Chair. First Vice-Chair: Arvind Panagariya; now Suman Bery (from 2022). Policy think-tank, NOT a fund-allocation body.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The LAST Five-Year Plan of India was the:
questions.explanation: 12th FYP (2012-2017) — last five-year plan. Theme: 'Faster, Sustainable and More Inclusive Growth'. After NITI Aayog replaced Planning Commission (2015), the 5-year-plan framework was replaced with a 3-year Action Agenda (2017-2020), 7-year Strategy, and 15-year Vision document.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The 'GOLDEN QUADRILATERAL' highway project aims to connect:
questions.explanation: GQ — National Highway project connecting Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata (~6,000 km). Initiated by NHAI under Vajpayee's NDA government (1998-99). Completed 2012. Reduced travel times + freight costs significantly. Part of NHDP (National Highways Development Project).
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The concept of 'GARIBI HATAO' was a central slogan of which PLAN?
questions.explanation: 5th FYP (1974-79) — 'Garibi Hatao' ('Remove Poverty') was its central theme, coined during Indira Gandhi's 1971 election campaign. Emphasis on employment, poverty alleviation. Also Minimum Needs Programme (MNP). Terminated early by Janata government in 1978, 1 year ahead.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: PLANNING COMMISSION was set up under the chairmanship of:
questions.explanation: Planning Commission — set up 15 March 1950 by a Cabinet resolution. PM ex-officio Chairperson. Nehru as first chair. Gulzarilal Nanda — first deputy chairman. Mahalanobis — statistician (designed 2nd plan model). Montek Singh Ahluwalia — longest-serving deputy chair (2004-14). as PM, ex-officio Chairman.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The period between India's Third and Fourth Five-Year Plans is called a 'Plan Holiday'. During which years were Annual Plans implemented instead of a regular Five-Year Plan?

options.option_text: 1962–65 (coinciding with the Third Five-Year Plan period)
1966–69 (gap between the Third and Fourth Five-Year Plans)
1971–74 (initial phase before the Fifth Five-Year Plan)
1979–80 (transition year before the Sixth Five-Year Plan)

questions.explanation: B is correct: after the Third Plan (1961–66) ended, India faced severe economic stress from the 1962 Sino-Indian War, 1965 Indo-Pak War, and back-to-back droughts, leading to three Annual Plans (1966–67, 1967–68, 1968–69) before the Fourth Plan began in 1969. Option D (1979–80) is a common distractor — though the Janata government disrupted planning, that period had a Sixth Plan launch attempt, not a formal 'Plan Holiday'.

questions.stem: Which government introduced the 'Rolling Plan' system in India, replacing the conventional fixed five-year planning cycle, and during which period was it operative?

options.option_text: Indira Gandhi's Congress government, operative during 1974–79
Rajiv Gandhi's Congress government, operative during 1985–90
Morarji Desai's Janata Party government, operative during 1978–83
V.P. Singh's National Front government, operative during 1990–95

questions.explanation: C is correct: PM Morarji Desai's Janata government (1977–79) rejected the rigid Five-Year Plan model and introduced rolling plans for 1978–83, where annual targets were revised each year. When Indira Gandhi returned in 1980 she abandoned rolling plans and launched the conventional Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980–85). Option A is wrong — Indira Gandhi was an architect of Five-Year Plans, not rolling plans.

questions.stem: The 'Minimum Needs Programme' (MNP), which guaranteed basic services like primary education, rural health, and drinking water to the poorest sections, was first introduced in which Five-Year Plan?

options.option_text: Third Five-Year Plan (1961–66), centred on self-reliance
Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969–74), focused on growth with stability
Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974–79), prioritising poverty alleviation
Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980–85), targeting Integrated Rural Development

questions.explanation: C is correct: the MNP was a flagship innovation of the Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974–79) under PM Indira Gandhi, providing guaranteed universal access to seven basic social services. Option D (6th Plan) is the most tempting distractor because the 6th Plan also emphasised rural poverty through IRDP — but MNP originated in the 5th Plan and was merely continued and expanded thereafter.

questions.stem: The Gadgil-Mukherjee Formula, revised in 1990, is primarily used to determine which of the following in Indian fiscal federalism?

options.option_text: Division of GST revenues between the Centre and States post-2017
Distribution of central plan assistance and grants among individual states
Criteria for fund allocation under the MGNREGS wage component
Calculation of states' share in the Finance Commission devolution pool

questions.explanation: B is correct: the Gadgil Formula (1969, revised by Mukherjee in 1990) governed how the Planning Commission split Central Assistance for State Plans, weighting population (60%), per-capita income (10%), tax effort (10%), special problems (10%), and plan performance (10%). Option D (Finance Commission devolution) is the most tempting error — Finance Commission and Planning Commission transfers were entirely separate channels with different criteria.

questions.stem: The Twelfth Five-Year Plan (2012–17) originally targeted 9% GDP growth in its Approach Paper but the National Development Council revised it downward. What was the approved target and what primarily forced the revision?

options.option_text: Revised to 7%; primarily caused by collapse of agricultural output in 2012
Revised to 8%; driven by global financial slowdown and India's fiscal stress
Revised to 8.5%; triggered by sharp depreciation of the Indian rupee in 2011
Revised to 7.5%; caused by contraction in India's export-oriented IT sector

questions.explanation: B is correct: the NDC in December 2012 approved an 8% growth target (down from 9%) citing post-2008 global financial uncertainty, high current account deficit, and fiscal consolidation pressures. Options A and D (7% and 7.5%) are numerical traps for candidates who recall 'it was revised down' but not the exact figure. The rupee depreciation in option C was a symptom of the broader stress, not the primary planning factor driving the NDC decision.

questions.stem: India's Five-Year Plans frequently missed growth targets in the early decades. Which Plan period was the FIRST to sustain an average real GDP growth rate exceeding 7% throughout its complete duration?

options.option_text: Seventh Plan (1985–90), boosted by Rajiv Gandhi's technology push
Eighth Plan (1992–97), driven by post-liberalisation reform momentum
Tenth Plan (2002–07), powered by IT, services sector and manufacturing
Eleventh Plan (2007–12), buoyed by strong global high-growth tailwinds

questions.explanation: C is correct: the Tenth Plan (2002–07) achieved approximately 7.6–7.7% average GDP growth — the first plan to sustain over 7% — powered by IT exports, services sector expansion, and domestic consumption. Option B (8th Plan) is the most tempting distractor because it is celebrated as India's first post-reform success plan, but it averaged only about 6.7%, below the 7% mark. The 11th Plan also exceeded 7% but was second, not first.

questions.stem: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission's Five-Year Plans with a three-tier planning architecture announced in 2017. Which option correctly identifies the time horizon of each tier?
questions.explanation: C is correct: NITI Aayog's 2017 framework comprises (i) a 15-Year Vision Document (2017–2032), (ii) a 7-Year National Development Strategy (2017–2024), and (iii) a 3-Year Action Agenda (2017–2020). Options B and D are crafted to catch candidates who recall '15-year and 7-year' correctly but guess '5-year' for the short-term tier (anchored on the old Five-Year Plan habit) or inflate the Action Agenda to 5 years instead of 3.
